Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs - Shoply

Hi Alice / Ben —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps we discussed. Please flag anything I missed or mischaracterized.

High-level goal
- Migrate Shoply away from proprietary LLM APIs (OpenAI / Anthropic) to an open-model stack that preserves current feature set and improves unit economics.

Key pain points you shared
- Cost: current spend on OpenAI/Anthropic embeddings + chat is high and unpredictable given traffic spikes.
- Latency: some search/assistant flows need consistent sub-200ms tail latency.
- Vendor lock & feature compatibility: existing product relies on OpenAI-style APIs (function calling, streaming, embeddings).
- Compliance/data residency: need control over data flow and audit logs for EU and US customers.

Current stack (from what you described)
- Inference: OpenAI (chat + embeddings) + occasional Anthropic for longer-form generation.
- Orchestration: Kubernetes on GCP, Terraform.
- Auth: Google SSO, secrets in GCP KMS.
- Observability: internal tracing + Datadog.

Success criteria for a migration PoC
- API compatibility: drop-in parity for chat endpoints, streaming, and embeddings to avoid rewriting client code.
- Quality: responses match or exceed current average relevance / helpfulness metrics on our test prompts.
- Cost: >= 35-40% reduction in per-token/embedding unit cost at target QPS.
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for critical assistant routes.
- Security: ability to run in VPC and integrate with customer KMS + SSO.

Compatibility needs we called out
- OpenAI-compatible REST surface (chat, completions, embeddings) including streaming and function/tool calling.
- Support for model routing and fallbacks (smaller local models for cheap, larger cloud models for quality).
- Embedding dimension parity / migration mapping for your vector DB.

Initial model shortlist (for PoC)
- Llama 2 / Meta-compatible instruction-tuned variants (7B / 13B)
- Mistral Instruct (7B) for cost-efficient responses
- Falcon 40B/180B for higher-quality generation in cloud-hosted config
- RedPajama-INCITE / TII variants for embeddings/local inference

Attachments sent
- Shoply-security-questionnaire.pdf (please review, will populate answers next)
- migration-playbook-draft.xlsx (high-level PoC plan and success metrics)

Next steps (agreed)
1) Shoply to confirm regulatory/residency constraints + internal stakeholders (security, infra, PM) — Alice
2) Redwood to fill out security questionnaire and share a PoC plan + timing — Marissa (attached)
3) Schedule 60m PoC kickoff with infra + security (target week of Aug 24) — propose Wed/Thu
4) Quick technical demo of Redwood Dedicated and Private routing (Marissa + Rishi) — target next week

If that looks accurate, I’ll schedule the demo and kick off the questionnaire answers.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful and accurately captures today's conversation. A few clarifications from our side:

- Data residency: for EU customers we need tenant-aware routing and residency in eu-west-1 or our EU cluster.
- KMS / Key ownership: we require BYOK for any customer data at rest (GCP KMS or a customer HSM).
- SSO: SAML/Okta is a hard requirement.

Ben from infra is looping in details (cc'd). He also asked whether Redwood has a migration path for existing embedding vectors (dimension parity & retraining notes) — we can share a sample vector set if helpful.

Confirming availability for a short demo next Tue or Thu afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Alice Chen
